Re: Expedited/Standard Member Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Jordan Kimura  
Member ID: W450262274  
Reference number: POC-9297E0E467-45895  
Requested service: Bunion surgery for hallux valgus  
CPT: 28296  
Date of denial notice: August 25, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296, correction of hallux valgus with bunionectomy. The denial notice identifies the reason for denial as insufficient imaging support for medical necessity.

The submitted records support the medical necessity of surgery:

- I have experienced 18 months of progressive foot pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed conservative treatment from May 19, 2026, through July 14, 2026, including activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic. The physical therapy discharge note documents 20 completed visits.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 7, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- Weight-bearing foot radiographs obtained July 26, 2026, objectively demonstrate hallux valgus, with a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- The deformity causes substantial functional impairment. I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and the prominence creates a risk of ulceration.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- There is no active infection. I am a nonsmoker, have a BMI of 29, and have no untreated substance-use issue documented in the records.
- The requested procedure is being recommended by Marchetti, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, after failure of prolonged conservative treatment.

The radiographs are weight-bearing and provide objective angular measurements of the deformity. The 38-degree hallux valgus angle and 17-degree intermetatarsal angle, combined with persistent pain, impaired shoe tolerance, limited painful motion, ulceration risk, and failure of conservative treatment, directly address whether the deformity is clinically significant and whether continued nonsurgical care has been effective.

I request that MedStar Family Choice overturn the denial and approve CPT 28296. If the denial is maintained, please provide the exact medical-necessity criteria, guideline or utilization-management standard, version, and effective date applied to this request, including the specific imaging requirements and the precise reason the July 26, 2026, weight-bearing radiographs were considered insufficient.

No payer medical-policy text has been quoted in this appeal because a publicly available MedStar Family Choice policy containing the applicable CPT 28296 criteria was not identified. Please therefore evaluate this appeal using the actual criteria applied to this case and provide those criteria with the reconsideration decision.

Please also confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Jordan Kimura
